t: You're on Victoria Road, a street in the London Borough of Brent. It takes its name from Queen Victoria, who reigned from 1837 to 1901, longer than any monarch before her. Her sixty-three years on the throne gave their name to the Victorian era, a period of industrial, political, scientific and military change, during which the British Empire expanded greatly. In 1876, Parliament also voted her the title of Empress of India. There's little else on record here, but the name ties this ordinary street to that long reign.
